title: The CEO’s Case for Local Civic Engagement
gist: BCG argues, from interviews with 35-plus CEOs and community leaders, that local civic engagement has become a hard-nosed talent-and-trust play rather than philanthropy, at a moment when city budgets are flat, housing costs have jumped (mortgage-to-income across 80 large cities went from 48% in 2021 to 64% in 2025) and BCG expects AI to reshape 50-55% of US roles within three years with disruption concentrated in white-collar metros. The practical edge is the reframing of community spend as backlash-proof substitute for national advocacy, plus quantified payoffs: 2.5x value creation for most-trusted firms and 52% lower early-tenure turnover for purpose-program participants.

insights.claim: Across 80 large cities worldwide, the average share of mortgage payments relative to household disposable income rose from 48% in 2021 to 64% in 2025, according to BCG analysis.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A 16-point jump in housing burden in four years is a leading indicator of local political pressure on rents, zoning and wages — watch homebuilders, mortgage servicers and municipal credit in the most stressed metros.

insights.claim: US city budgets have stopped growing: spending levels for a group of 200-plus American cities were flat in 2025 after pandemic-era federal assistance (ARPA-style funds) was phased out, per the National League of Cities.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Flat municipal spending after the stimulus cliff means fewer local contracts and grants — a headwind for vendors selling into city governments and for muni-backed local services.
insights.quote: spending levels for a group of 200-plus cities were flat in 2025 after the phaseout of pandemic era assistance
insights.locator: Yet the resources available to help communities adapt

insights.claim: Corporate money is not filling the municipal gap: median total company community investments — cash donations, pro bono work and in-kind support — grew only 5% between 2022 and 2024 according to benchmarking group Chief Executives for Corporate Purpose.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A 5% two-year rise is below cumulative inflation, so real corporate community spend has shrunk — expect the gap to be met with non-cash contributions (expertise, infrastructure) rather than checks.
insights.quote: were up a modest 5% between 2022 and 2024
insights.locator: Company financial contributions, meanwhile, are unlikely

insights.claim: BCG estimates that 50% to 55% of roles in the US will be reshaped by AI within the next two to three years, and that 10% to 15% could be displaced over the next five years.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A concrete, dated displacement range to benchmark staffing, payroll-services and consumer-credit exposure against; the 10-15% displacement tail is the number to stress-test.
insights.quote: 50% to 55% of roles in the US will be reshaped by AI in the next two to three years, and 10% to 15% could be displaced over the next five years
insights.locator: For example, while the timeline for change is unclear

insights.claim: AI job disruption is expected to be geographically concentrated in places with high shares of information, finance, professional services, and clerical and administrative roles, rather than spread evenly across the country.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Implies white-collar metros — not manufacturing towns — carry the next displacement shock, with knock-on risk to local tax bases, CRE and regional bank loan books in those cities.
insights.quote: The disruption from these changes could be concentrated in specific geographies
insights.locator: This impact could increase pressure on local workforce systems

themes.theme: Trust as a measurable value multiple

insights.claim: BCG's Trust Index research found that the most trusted companies generated roughly 2.5 times more value creation than market-average companies.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Puts a quantified multiple on an intangible: trust screens can be used as a factor overlay, and trust damage as a repricing trigger.
insights.quote: the most trusted companies generated approximately 2.5 times more value creation than market-average companies
insights.locator: Trust. Trust is a clear benefit of civic engagement

insights.claim: Executives describe local civic involvement as buying access to decision-making rooms: helping with community problems earns a seat alongside the business and government leaders shaping a city.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Reframes community spend as regulatory and permitting access — most valuable for firms whose economics depend on local approvals (real estate, utilities, healthcare, logistics).
insights.quote: If you spend time helping address challenges facing the local community, you’ve earned the right to be in the room with business and government leaders shaping the city
insights.locator: notes the CEO of the technology firm

insights.claim: Global workforce engagement is at a low ebb, with just 20% of workers worldwide reporting being engaged in 2025 according to Gallup.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: An 80% disengaged workforce is a productivity drag that AI deployment alone will not fix — vendors and programs targeting engagement have a large addressable problem.
insights.quote: just 20% of workers worldwide reported being engaged in 2025, according to Gallup
insights.locator: The employee engagement upside alone is sorely needed

insights.claim: According to enterprise social impact software provider Benevity, turnover among employees with two and a half years of tenure or less is 52% lower for those who participate in corporate purpose programs.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A 52% retention delta on early-tenure staff is a direct cost-of-hiring saving; note the source is a vendor selling the software, so the causal direction (self-selection vs. program effect) is unproven.
insights.quote: turnover among newer employees (those who have been with the company two and half years or less) is 52% lower for those who participate in corporate purpose programs
insights.locator: While it is intuitive that caring about the places

insights.claim: Senior executives use community board service as a cheap, low-risk assessment environment for evaluating up-and-coming leaders, because working inside one company is a closed environment that hides how a person influences and leads outside their authority.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A non-obvious succession-planning signal: external board placements of internal candidates can be read as a tell for who is being groomed.
insights.quote: Serving on a [community] board is an important part of leadership development. It shows someone can influence and engage more broadly

themes.theme: Local engagement as backlash-proof substitute for national advocacy

insights.claim: Corporate leadership has shifted from the outspoken public advocacy of the late 2010s and early 2020s to a cautious, restrained stance, and local results-oriented engagement is being positioned as the way to keep visible impact while avoiding the backlash of polarizing national debates.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Expect corporate social spend to be relabeled and relocalized rather than cut — watch for 'community' and 'workforce' framing replacing ESG/DEI language in filings and shareholder letters.
insights.quote: Focusing on local, results-oriented engagement offers a way to drive meaningful impact while avoiding the backlash that comes with wading into polarizing national debates
insights.locator: The Business Case for Local Civic Engagement

insights.claim: CEOs face increased scrutiny from boards and shareholders over diverting leadership attention and money to initiatives that do not contribute directly to near-term shareholder returns, which is actively dampening corporate community investment.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Confirms investor pressure, not ideology, is the binding constraint on corporate social spend — programs must now be justified on talent and trust P&L terms or be cut.
insights.quote: increased scrutiny from boards and shareholders on efforts to divert leadership attention and financial resources toward initiatives that do not contribute directly to near-term shareholder returns

insights.claim: Structural corporate trends have severed local roots: globalization and remote work diffuse company footprints, while elevated M&A activity and centralization of philanthropy strategies away from a local lens further weaken community ties.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: M&A and remote-work adoption predict which communities lose corporate anchor support — a screen for local economies facing quiet withdrawal of private funding.
insights.quote: elevated M&A activity and a shift toward more centralized corporate philanthropy strategies (with less of a local lens), further weaken those connections

themes.theme: Five-level engagement spectrum and governance design

insights.claim: A five-level spectrum classifies corporate community activity — initial actions (volunteer hours, donation matching), targeted engagement (one-off drives and sponsorships), core business integration (workforce training, local sourcing, supply chains), shared stewardship (board seats, task forces), and civic leadership (convening power, policy engagement, philanthropic capital) — with competitive advantage only appearing from level three upward where the activity is embedded in the operating model.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A diagnostic to sort genuine operating-model integration from PR: only levels 3-5 touch the P&L, so treat level 1-2 disclosures as marketing.
insights.quote: Our conversations with business and community leaders revealed a five-level spectrum
insights.locator: What Civic Engagement Looks Like in Practice

insights.claim: The recommended governance fix is to give non-headquarters sites their own authority to invest in locally relevant efforts, reversing the centralization of corporate giving that the same research blames for weakening community ties.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: Budget decentralization is the observable tell that a company's community strategy is real; centralized giving programs are the ones most likely to be cut in a downturn.
insights.quote: gives non-headquarters sites ability to invest in locally relevant efforts, and reduces diffuse, fragmented efforts

insights.claim: Effective programs deliberately narrow scope to a few issues matched to in-house expertise and commit on a five- to ten-year horizon, treating institutional knowledge of a place as the compounding asset rather than the dollar amount deployed.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A five-to-ten year commitment horizon is far longer than typical CEO tenure — programs that survive a CEO change are the ones actually embedded in the business.
insights.quote: They commit to the long term, taking a five- to ten-year time horizon

insights.claim: Michelin converted a century-old decommissioned production site in Clermont-Ferrand into a €300 million innovation district with more than 50 public and private partners, comprising training centers, a hybrid coworking and events real estate complex, a museum, an urban farm and a jazz club, targeting 400,000 visitors a year.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: A template for monetizing legacy industrial land: brownfield-to-mixed-use conversion funded through partnership rather than balance sheet, and a real precedent for other legacy manufacturers sitting on obsolete sites.
insights.quote: partnered with over 50 public and private organizations transform a century-old, decommissioned production site into a €300 million innovation district

insights.claim: Retail technology company Shipt addresses US food access — where over 40 million people live with limited access to fresh food — through an eight-week LadderUp Accelerator plus more than 80 Community Impact Grants totaling nearly $1.3 million over four years, enabling more than 2.3 million meals.
insights.speaker: BCG Henderson Institute
insights.so_what: The absolute dollars (~$325k a year) are tiny relative to the 40-million-person problem framing — a useful calibration of how small headline corporate impact programs often are versus their communications footprint.
insights.quote: Shipt has awarded more than 80 Community Impact Grants totaling nearly $1.3 million, helping enable more than 2.3 million meals for over half-a-million food-insecure individuals
insights.locator: Retail technology company Shipt has also leveraged
